title: Procurement purchase-to-pay: the simulated organization reproduces 2018 operations
subtitle: BPI Challenge 2019 instance, 13 weekly held-out cutoffs, 14-day horizon
takeaways: The simulated workforce completes 71.2% of open items within 14 days against 69.8% observed, 16 points above the persistence baseline.
Payment-block rate is reproduced within 1.3 points (21.8% simulated vs 23.1% actual).
An automated three-way match within 2% tolerance cuts payment blocks from 54 to 12 per run and removes 249 labor hours per fortnight.
Cutting accounts payable by 20% pushes median cycle time from 9.8 to 12.6 days; the queue does not recover within the horizon.

sections.heading: What was simulated
sections.body:
Every purchase-order line item open at a weekly cutoff **t0** is continued for 14 simulated days by 607 agents in five roles bound to O*NET occupations. Arrivals replay the observed stream; every decision inside the firm is produced by the kernel and the seat policies.

- Buyers and purchasing managers are rule seats calibrated on the training window.
- Accounts payable clerks are an LLM seat (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) that sees the invoice, PO and goods-receipt documents.
- Nightly clearing is a batch seat.

sections.heading: Accuracy against the held-out weeks
sections.body: The queue trajectory tracks the observed one across all thirteen cutoffs; the largest miss is 1.9 points on the week of October 8. Scatter per spend area shows no systematic bias: the fit line has slope 0.97.

sections.heading: What the interventions do
sections.body: Two interventions were run on the same seeds. The automated match is a capability added to the SAP system node; the headcount cut is a parameter on the AP role. Both change the simulated work process without touching any instance code.
